editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally, and it keeps the overwrite caveat in [10] ("Esse método sobrescreve as tags atuais... certifique-se de reatribuir as tags originais"). It uses "tags de job", "submeter um job" and "mitigação de erros" consistently, in casual "você".

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. ZNE, PEA, PEC, TREX, OBP and PNA keep their claims intact, including PEC's "unbiased estimate at the expense of greater overhead", and valor esperado, observável and mitigação/supressão de erros are used consistently. In [15], "Está escrito nos padrões modernos C++17" is a calque; "Foi escrito seguindo o padrão C++17" reads more naturally.

examples.suggested: Técnica de modelagem do ruído que transforma qualquer canal de ruído

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the last 40%. The billing rules in [32] ("o que ocorrer **por último**"), [52] and [64] are all intact, and so are the worked example with 5 lanes, 2 busy and 3 of 6 jobs started ([55]-[56]) and the yes/no answers on interruption in [30] and [62]. Two phrasings are stiff enough that a native editor would change them. In [32], "**committed to the session**" became "**comprometido com a sessão**", which reads as loyalty rather than resource allocation, so "alocado/dedicado à sessão" is better. In [5], the title "O modo de teste local `qiskit-ibm-runtime`" puts the package name awkwardly as an apposition. Terminology is consistent: jobs, backend, lote, faixas de execução, agendador, TTL interativo.

examples.why: In Portuguese, 'comprometido com' means being committed or loyal to something. It is not how you say a resource is allocated or reserved, so 'dedicado/alocado à sessão' is the natural term here.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and I found no drift that would mislead a learner. Caveats such as "no library is linked", "Python is not used at runtime" and "qiskit-aer is optional" all survive intact. The problems are consistency and polish. Terms switch between renderings: "UNIX-like" appears as "do tipo UNIX" [8], "semelhante ao UNIX" [27] and untranslated "UNIX-like" [80]. editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the closing caveat in [42] that the outer-loop expansion "ainda não foi implementado", so nothing would mislead a learner. A native ML editor would still change a few things. The ML metric "accuracy" is rendered as "precisão" in [11], [39], [40] and the benchmark table [41], but in Portuguese ML usage "precisão" normally means the separate precision metric; "acurácia" is the conventional term. There are also some stiff spots: "consegue consistentemente alta precisão" in [11] is missing its verb, "demonstra … e demonstra" repeats in [12], and "semicírculos entrelaçados" in [12]/[20] uses the word that means "entangled" in a quantum text, where "intercalados" is clearer.

examples.source: "Classical accuracy" refers to the accuracy obtained using corresponding classical state of the art
examples.translation: "Precisão clássica" refere-se à precisão obtida usando o estado da arte clássico correspondente
examples.suggested: "Acurácia clássica" refere-se à acurácia obtida usando o estado da arte clássico correspondente
examples.why: In ML, accuracy and precision are different metrics. 'Acurácia' is the standard pt-BR term for accuracy, and 'precisão' suggests the precision metric. The same fix applies in [11], [39] and the table headers in [41].

examples.source: It consistently achieves high accuracies on classically challenging problems
examples.translation: Ela consegue consistentemente alta precisão em problemas classicamente desafiadores
examples.suggested: Ela atinge consistentemente alta acurácia em problemas classicamente desafiadores
examples.why: 'Consegue alta precisão' has no main verb such as 'alcançar' or 'atingir' and reads as broken machine translation.

examples.source: The following example showcases its various functionalities ... and demonstrates its usage in a synthetic problem comprising two interleaving half circles
examples.translation: O exemplo a seguir demonstra suas diversas funcionalidades ... e demonstra seu uso em um problema sintético composto por dois semicírculos entrelaçados
examples.suggested: O exemplo a seguir apresenta suas diversas funcionalidades ... e mostra seu uso em um problema sintético composto por dois semicírculos intercalados
examples.why: Repeating 'demonstra' twice reads robotic. In a quantum text, 'entrelaçados' is the word for 'entangled', so 'intercalados' avoids the false association. The same applies in [20].

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. Qubit counts, dates, revisions and the Eagle/Egret/Osprey lineage all match, and nothing would mislead a learner. There are two small phrasing issues. In [3], "tradeoffs" becomes the wordy paraphrase "trocas entre diferentes atributos", where the usual Portuguese term is "compromissos" (trade-offs). In [16], the adjectives "rápido e de alta fidelidade" sit after "qubit único", so they seem to describe only the qubit instead of the control; putting them right after "controle" fixes this.

examples.source: often leading to performance improvements or tradeoffs
examples.translation: geralmente resultando em melhorias de desempenho ou em trocas entre diferentes atributos
examples.suggested: geralmente resultando em melhorias de desempenho ou em compromissos (trade-offs)

examples.why: 'escala' used as a verb for resizing an image sounds stiff. 'redimensiona' is the usual word.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. Alice's conditional Z/X gates in [10]-[11], Bob's CNOT and Hadamard with the correct control and target in [13], the four cd cases in [22]-[25] and the Holevo caveat in [5] all match the English. The one thing a native editor would change is in [4]: "ao custo de um e-bit por cima" is a clumsy rendering of "at the cost of an e-bit no less". The natural idiom is "ainda por cima", placed before the cost. Terms are consistent, with codificação superdensa, entrelaçamento, estado de Bell and lowercase "gate" used the same way throughout, and the register stays in casual "você".

examples.source: trading one qubit of quantum communication for two bits of classical communication, at the cost of an e-bit no less, hardly seems worth it
examples.translation: trocar um qubit de comunicação quântica por dois bits de comunicação clássica, ao custo de um e-bit por cima, mal parece valer a pena
examples.suggested: trocar um qubit de comunicação quântica por dois bits de comunicação clássica, e ainda por cima ao custo de um e-bit, mal parece valer a pena
examples.why: 'por cima' on its own after the noun phrase reads like a literal calque of 'no less'. The idiomatic intensifier is 'ainda por cima', placed before the cost.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and would not mislead a learner. The independence proof in [59], the marginal and conditional probability discussion in [109]-[116] and the CNOT and tensor-product sections all keep their meaning, and the terms are consistent (produto cartesiano, produto tensorial, estado produto, vetor de probabilidade, matriz estocástica). A native editor would still fix four things. [10] uses "Se supormos", which is ungrammatical; it should be "Se supusermos". [105] has a markup slip, "ou seja$,0$", where the comma was pulled inside the math delimiter. [192] drops the qualifier "sometimes" ("Diz-se que…" instead of "Às vezes se diz que…"). [156]/[157] use the calque "Defina Y para ser igual a X".

examples.source: If we suppose that $\mathsf{X}_1,\ldots,\mathsf{X}_n$ are systems
examples.translation: Se supormos que $\mathsf{X}_1,\ldots,\mathsf{X}_n$ são sistemas
examples.suggested: Se supusermos que $\mathsf{X}_1,\ldots,\mathsf{X}_n$ são sistemas
examples.why: 'supor' needs the future subjunctive 'supusermos'. 'supormos' is a common but incorrect form in edited technical text.

examples.source: — meaning $0$ for the measurement of $\mathsf{X}$
examples.translation: — ou seja$,0$ para a medição de $\mathsf{X}$
examples.suggested: — ou seja, $0$ para a medição de $\mathsf{X}$
examples.why: The comma was moved inside the math delimiter and the space was lost, so it renders as 'ou seja,0'.

examples.source: The tensor product of matrices is sometimes said to be *multiplicative* because the equation
examples.translation: Diz-se que o produto tensorial de matrizes é *multiplicativo* porque a equação
examples.suggested: Às vezes se diz que o produto tensorial de matrizes é *multiplicativo* porque a equação
examples.why: Drops the qualifier 'sometimes', which makes a loose naming habit sound like standard terminology. The math is unaffected.

examples.source: Set $\mathsf{Y}$ to be equal to $\mathsf{X}$.
examples.translation: Defina $\mathsf{Y}$ para ser igual a $\mathsf{X}$.
examples.suggested: Faça $\mathsf{Y}$ igual a $\mathsf{X}$.
examples.why: This copies the English 'set … to be' structure word for word. A Portuguese technical writer would write 'Faça Y igual a X' or 'Atribua a Y o valor de X'.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The meaning holds throughout, and core terms are correct and used consistently: estado produto, emaranhados, base de Bell, medição na base padrão, subconjunto próprio, conjugado transposto. There are still a few things an editor would fix. "Simplesmente dito" in [173] is a calque of "Simply put". In [147] and [169] a comma was moved inside the math delimiter ("por exemplo$,U^{\dagger}..."), so it renders with no space after the comma. In [90], the neutral "becomes" was translated as "colapsa para", which brings in the collapse idea one paragraph before the source does.

examples.source: Simply put, Dirac notation is not always the best choice.
examples.translation: Simplesmente dito, a notação de Dirac nem sempre é a melhor escolha.
examples.suggested: Em suma, a notação de Dirac nem sempre é a melhor escolha.
examples.why: 'Simplesmente dito' is a word-for-word calque of 'Simply put' that a Portuguese writer would not use.

examples.source: it suffices to compute and check that $U^{\dagger} U = \mathbb{I}$, for instance.
examples.translation: basta calcular e verificar que, por exemplo$,U^{\dagger} U = \mathbb{I}$.
examples.suggested: basta, por exemplo, calcular e verificar que $U^{\dagger} U = \mathbb{I}$.
examples.why: The comma was moved inside the math delimiter, so the text renders as 'por exemplo,U†U' with no space. Entry [147] has the same glitch ('por exemplo$,(\heartsuit,\diamondsuit)$').

examples.source: the quantum state of the pair $(\mathsf{X},\mathsf{Y})$ together becomes
examples.translation: o estado quântico do par $(\mathsf{X},\mathsf{Y})$ colapsa para
examples.suggested: o estado quântico do par $(\mathsf{X},\mathsf{Y})$ passa a ser
examples.why: The source uses the neutral 'becomes' and brings in 'collapses' only in the next entry, in scare quotes. The translation uses collapse one step early. This is harmless but less faithful.

examples.source: Quantum information
examples.translation: Informação Quântica
examples.suggested: Informação quântica
examples.why: The heading uses English-style title case. Every other heading in the file uses Portuguese sentence case (e.g. 'Estados quânticos', 'Medições parciais').

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The translation is faithful, and it handles idioms such as "equivalentes a menos de uma fase global" and "lei dos grandes números" well. A native editor would still change four things. The lesson title "single-systems" is rendered as "sistemas de um único elemento", which reads as "single-element systems". "qubit state vector(s)" is rendered twice as "vetor(es) de estado quântico", which drops the qubit qualifier. Two sentences are stiff calques: "não serão formalmente introduzidos até a aula…" in [44] and "resulta no resultado" in [35].

examples.source: ideas from the single-systems lesson
examples.translation: conceitos da aula sobre sistemas de um único elemento
examples.suggested: conceitos da aula sobre sistemas únicos (Sistemas individuais)
examples.why: 'Single systems' means one system considered on its own. 'Um único elemento' suggests the system has only one element, and that does not match the lesson title.

examples.source: corresponding to the qubit state vectors |0> and |1>
examples.translation: correspondentes aos vetores de estado quântico |0> e |1>
examples.suggested: correspondentes aos vetores de estado do qubit |0> e |1>
examples.why: This drops 'qubit', and [25] does the same with 'vetor de estado quântico v'. The English deliberately says these are qubit states.

examples.source: Quantum circuits won't be formally introduced until the Quantum circuits lesson
examples.translation: Os circuitos quânticos não serão formalmente introduzidos até a aula de Circuitos quânticos
examples.suggested: Os circuitos quânticos só serão introduzidos formalmente na aula de Circuitos quânticos
examples.why: 'Não ... até' is a calque of the English 'won't ... until'. Native Portuguese uses 'só ... na'.

examples.source: which (with high probability) results in the outcome 0 approximately 5 out of every 9 times
examples.translation: o que (com alta probabilidade) resulta no resultado $0$ aproximadamente $5$ de cada $9$ vezes
examples.suggested: o que (com alta probabilidade) produz o resultado $0$ em aproximadamente $5$ de cada $9$ vezes
examples.why: 'Resulta no resultado' repeats the same word and reads clumsily.

editor_note: In entry [35], the global systems integrators section says the technical team needs expertise "either in quantum computing or in the application area". The Portuguese reads "tanto em computação quântica quanto na área de aplicação", which means both. That makes the staffing requirement stricter than the source, probably by copying the wording of [17]/[25], and it changes the hiring advice readers get. There are also smaller slips: [62] turns "next lessons" into the singular "próxima lição", [10] uses the calque "campeão quântico" for "quantum champion", and [52] uses the literal "escalarão para utilidade".

examples.source: They should have expertise either in quantum computing or in the application area of the client.
examples.translation: Eles devem ter expertise tanto em computação quântica quanto na área de aplicação do cliente.
examples.suggested: Eles devem ter expertise em computação quântica ou na área de aplicação do cliente.
examples.why: 'either...or' became 'both...and', so a requirement where one skill is enough now demands both, which misstates the staffing guidance for integrators.

examples.source: In the next lessons, we address promoting your team's abilities to outside groups.
examples.translation: Na próxima lição, abordamos a promoção das capacidades da sua equipe para grupos externos.
examples.suggested: Nas próximas lições, abordamos como divulgar as capacidades da sua equipe para grupos externos.
examples.why: Plural 'lessons' became singular; minor, but it misdescribes the course structure.

examples.source: Establish a internal quantum champion to advocate for quantum computing
examples.translation: Estabeleça um campeão quântico interno para defender a computação quântica
examples.suggested: Designe um defensor (ou promotor) interno da computação quântica para apoiar a área
examples.why: 'Campeão' is a calque of the business sense of 'champion'. In Portuguese corporate writing, 'defensor' or 'promotor' is more natural.

examples.source: they will not scale to utility
examples.translation: eles não escalarão para utilidade
examples.suggested: eles não escalam até a escala de utilidade
examples.why: Literal rendering; 'utility' here means utility-scale quantum computing, which the phrase 'para utilidade' does not convey.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout: nothing inverts, drops or adds a claim, and the core terms are correct and consistent (síndrome, matriz de densidade, estado produto, projetamos, representação de Kraus). There are three wording problems. In [43] the relative clause "que armazena a codificação" is separated from "sistema", so it reads as if the "processo" stores the encoding. In [42] "correspondentemente diferentes síndromes" copies the English word order and reads awkwardly. In [29] the channel names are left in English as "canal de dephasing ou depolarizing", where Portuguese technical writing would say "defasagem"/"despolarizante".

examples.source: thereby removing the randomness generated in this process from the system that stores the encoding.
examples.translation: removendo assim do sistema a aleatoriedade gerada neste processo que armazena a codificação.
examples.suggested: removendo assim a aleatoriedade gerada neste processo do sistema que armazena a codificação.
examples.why: The relative clause 'que armazena a codificação' now attaches to 'processo' instead of 'sistema'. A careful reader can work out the intended meaning, but the sentence is ambiguous and clumsy.

examples.source: and correspondingly different syndromes specify Pauli operation corrections
examples.translation: e correspondentemente diferentes síndromes especificam correções de operações de Pauli
examples.suggested: e, de modo correspondente, síndromes diferentes especificam correções por operações de Pauli
examples.why: This copies the English word order. In Portuguese the adverb seems to modify 'diferentes', which makes the sentence stiff.

examples.source: this could be a dephasing or depolarizing channel, a reset channel
examples.translation: este poderia ser um canal de dephasing ou depolarizing, um canal de reset
examples.suggested: este poderia ser um canal de defasagem ou despolarizante, um canal de reset
examples.why: The channel names are left as English adjectives inside a Portuguese phrase. The usual Portuguese forms are 'canal de defasagem' and 'canal despolarizante'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The claims about the surface code, the rotated surface code, the color code and the [[144,12,12]] code carry over correctly, and 'gerador do estabilizador', 'código de superfície' and 'código de cor' are used consistently. A native editor would still change a few things. 'Gross code' became 'código grosso', which reads as 'thick/coarse code' and loses the gross = 144 meaning; 'código gross' or 'código grosa' would be better. 'tiles' is left in English in entries [10] and [25]. There are also two English calques: 'vamos arranhar a superfície' and 'Como se descobriu' for 'As it turns out'.

examples.source: Example: The gross code
examples.translation: Exemplo: O código grosso
examples.suggested: Exemplo: O código gross (gross code)
examples.why: The name 'gross' means a dozen dozen (144 = n). In Portuguese, 'grosso' means thick or coarse, so it misreads the name; the Portuguese word for that unit is 'grosa'. Keeping the English name is the safer choice.

examples.source: black tiles (including the rounded ones on the edges)
examples.translation: tiles pretos (incluindo os arredondados nas bordas)
examples.suggested: ladrilhos pretos (incluindo os arredondados nas bordas)
examples.why: 'tiles' is an ordinary word left in English, when Portuguese has natural equivalents such as ladrilhos or placas. The same thing happens again in entry [25].

examples.source: but we will scratch the surface just a bit
examples.translation: mas vamos arranhar a superfície um pouco
examples.suggested: mas vamos apenas tocar de leve no assunto
examples.why: This is a literal calque of an English idiom and sounds unnatural in Portuguese.

examples.source: As it turns out, it isn't actually necessary
examples.translation: Como se descobriu, não é estritamente necessário
examples.suggested: Na verdade, não é necessário
examples.why: 'Como se descobriu' is a stiff word-for-word rendering of 'As it turns out'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and none of it would mislead a learner. The promise, the two-to-one case, the 2^{n-1} range size, the k = n + 10 / 1 − 2^{-r} bounds and the classical lower bound of 2^{n/2−1}−1 all match the English, and the terms are well chosen (range→imagem, preimage→pré-imagem, null space→espaço nulo, one-to-one→injetora). The problems are a few English-shaped phrasings. "fazem a função avaliar para essa string de saída" in [36] and "vantagem exponencial do quantum sobre os algoritmos clássicos" in [4] and [78] read unnaturally. So do "não tem intenção de ter importância prática" in [10] and "da mesma forma ... como funciona" in [72]; a Brazilian technical editor would smooth all of these.

examples.source: all input strings that cause the function to evaluate to this output string $z$
examples.translation: todas as strings de entrada que fazem a função avaliar para essa string de saída $z$
examples.suggested: todas as strings de entrada para as quais a função assume o valor $z$
examples.why: 'avaliar para' copies the English 'evaluate to'. Portuguese says 'assumir o valor' or 'resultar em'.

examples.source: an *exponential* advantage of quantum over classical (including probabilistic) algorithms
examples.translation: uma vantagem *exponencial* do quantum sobre os algoritmos clássicos (incluindo probabilísticos)
examples.suggested: uma vantagem *exponencial* dos algoritmos quânticos sobre os clássicos (incluindo os probabilísticos)
examples.why: 'do quantum' as a bare noun is a calque. The same pattern appears again in [78].

examples.source: this problem isn't intended to have practical importance
examples.translation: esse problema não tem intenção de ter importância prática
examples.suggested: esse problema não pretende ter importância prática
examples.why: 'não tem intenção de ter' is stiff and repeats 'ter'.

examples.source: which works the same way when arithmetic is done modulo $2$ as it does with real or complex numbers
examples.translation: que funciona da mesma forma quando a aritmética é feita módulo $2$ como funciona com números reais ou complexos
examples.suggested: que funciona da mesma forma com aritmética módulo $2$ que com números reais ou complexos
examples.why: 'da mesma forma ... como funciona' copies the English 'the same way ... as it does'. Portuguese uses 'da mesma forma ... que'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The pole and angle descriptions, the antipodal orthogonal states, the Bloch ball and the completely mixed state at the center all match the English. Terminology is consistent: matriz densidade, esfera de Bloch, 2-esfera unitária, ângulo polar/azimutal, a menos de uma fase global. A native editor would still smooth a few English calques: "Em palavras" (entries 37 and 43), "unicamente determinados" (entry 7) and "ao variar sobre todos os estados" (entry 23).

examples.source: In words, $\vert +\rangle$ corresponds to the point where...
examples.translation: Em palavras, $\vert +\rangle$ corresponde ao ponto onde...
examples.suggested: Em outras palavras, $\vert +\rangle$ corresponde ao ponto em que...
examples.why: 'Em palavras' is a literal calque of 'In words'. Portuguese uses 'Em outras palavras' or 'Dito de outra forma'. The same calque appears in entry 43.

examples.source: it isn't quite the case that the numbers θ and φ are uniquely determined by a given quantum state vector
examples.translation: não é bem o caso de que os números θ e φ sejam unicamente determinados por um dado vetor
examples.suggested: não é bem verdade que os números θ e φ sejam determinados de forma única por um dado vetor
examples.why: 'não é bem o caso de que' and 'unicamente determinados' copy the English syntax. In Portuguese, 'unicamente' tends to read as 'only' rather than 'uniquely'.

examples.source: the points we obtain when we range over all possible pure states of a qubit
examples.translation: os pontos que obtemos ao variar sobre todos os estados puros possíveis de um qubit
examples.suggested: os pontos que obtemos ao percorrer todos os estados puros possíveis de um qubit
examples.why: 'variar sobre' is a calque of 'range over'. 'Percorrer' is the natural Portuguese verb here.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The explanations of trace, pure states, global phase and faithful representation all match the English, and "matriz de densidade", "traço", "autovalores" and "medição na base padrão" are used consistently. A native editor would still change four things. The lesson title "Single systems" is rendered "Sistemas simples", which means "simple systems", not "single systems". "Positive semidefinite" follows English word order as "positiva semidefinida"; Portuguese texts usually say "semidefinida positiva". "Hermitiana" is capitalized, where Portuguese normally writes it lowercase. In [9], the definitional "To say that ρ is a density matrix means…" becomes a weaker "Para que ρ seja… devem ser satisfeitas", which loses the if-and-only-if sense.

examples.source: here's a state from the *Single systems* lesson
examples.translation: aqui está um estado da aula *Sistemas simples*
examples.suggested: aqui está um estado da aula *Sistemas individuais*
examples.why: 'Simples' means 'simple', not 'single'. The title names the lesson on one system on its own.

examples.source: the property of a matrix being *positive semidefinite*
examples.translation: a propriedade de uma matriz ser *positiva semidefinida*
examples.suggested: a propriedade de uma matriz ser *semidefinida positiva*
examples.why: This keeps the English word order. Portuguese linear-algebra texts usually write 'matriz semidefinida positiva', and the same order appears in [18], [23]-[28].

examples.source: To say that $\rho$ is a density matrix means that these two conditions ... are both satisfied
examples.translation: Para que $\rho$ seja uma matriz de densidade, essas duas condições ... devem ser satisfeitas
examples.suggested: Dizer que $\rho$ é uma matriz de densidade significa que essas duas condições — que serão explicadas em breve — são ambas satisfeitas
examples.why: The English defines the term: ρ is a density matrix exactly when both conditions hold. The PT wording reads as a necessary condition only.

examples.source: $P$ is Hermitian
examples.translation: $P$ é Hermitiana
examples.suggested: $P$ é hermitiana
examples.why: In Portuguese, adjectives formed from proper names are written in lowercase.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the no-signalling argument in [42] and the partial-trace definitions, so nothing here would mislead a learner. There are four fixable slips. "density matrix" is "matriz densidade" in [3]–[14] but "matriz de densidade" from [29] onward. "ensemble" is "Conjuntos" in the [20] heading but "ensemble" in the body. "traced out" is calqued as "traçado fora" in [63], [65] and [95]. "happens to be" is calqued as "acontece de ser" in [43].

examples.source: Density matrix descriptions of reduced states...
examples.translation: Descrições em matriz de densidade dos estados reduzidos...
examples.suggested: Use one form throughout, either 'matriz densidade' (as in [3]–[14]) or 'matriz de densidade'
examples.why: The same core term appears in two forms in one file.

examples.source: or that $\mathsf{B}$ is *traced out*
examples.translation: ou que $\mathsf{B}$ é *traçado fora*
examples.suggested: ou que se *toma o traço parcial sobre* $\mathsf{B}$ (ou: $\mathsf{B}$ é *eliminado pelo traço*)
examples.why: 'traçado fora' is a literal calque of the English phrasal verb and doesn't read as idiomatic Portuguese.

examples.source: *Ensembles of quantum states.* ... an *ensemble* of states
examples.translation: *Conjuntos de estados quânticos.* ... um *ensemble* de estados
examples.suggested: *Ensembles de estados quânticos.*
examples.why: The heading and the defined term in the same paragraph use different words, which hides that they are the same concept.

examples.source: which happens to be the completely mixed state as well
examples.translation: que também acontece de ser o estado completamente misto
examples.suggested: que também é o estado completamente misto
examples.why: 'acontece de ser' is an anglicism calqued from 'happens to be'.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout: no inverted conditions, missing caveats or invented claims, and the conditional-state and partial-measurement sections ([112]–[149]) match the English closely. The problems are small. "density matrix" is mostly "matriz de densidade" but becomes "matrizes densidade" in [70] and [134]. A few phrases copy English wording, such as "é direto generalizar" / "direto de verificar" for "straightforward", "Traçando o sistema de saída" for "tracing out", "somam à matriz identidade", "com *finitos* resultados possíveis" and "canal qubit completamente defasante". A native editor would reword these.

examples.source: identify probabilistic states with diagonal density matrices
examples.translation: identificar estados probabilísticos com matrizes densidade diagonais
examples.suggested: identificar estados probabilísticos com matrizes de densidade diagonais
examples.why: The rest of the file uses 'matriz de densidade'. This entry and [134] drop the 'de'.

examples.source: Tracing out the output system Y (which is the system on the right) yields
examples.translation: Traçando o sistema de saída $\mathsf{Y}$ (que é o sistema à direita), obtemos
examples.suggested: Tomando o traço parcial sobre o sistema de saída $\mathsf{Y}$ (que é o sistema à direita), obtemos
examples.why: 'Traçando' copies the English 'tracing out'. In Portuguese the usual phrasing is 'tomar o traço parcial sobre'.

examples.source: it's straightforward to generalize everything that follows
examples.translation: é direto generalizar tudo que se segue
examples.suggested: é simples generalizar tudo o que se segue
examples.why: 'é direto' copies the English 'straightforward'. The same thing happens in [67]: 'tornam isso direto de verificar'.

examples.source: measurements having *finitely many* possible outcomes
examples.translation: medições com *finitos* resultados possíveis
examples.suggested: medições com um número *finito* de resultados possíveis
examples.why: 'com finitos resultados' is awkward in Portuguese. 'um número finito de' is the natural phrasing.

examples.source: the completely dephasing qubit channel Δ
examples.translation: canal qubit completamente defasante $\Delta$
examples.suggested: canal de qubit completamente defasante $\Delta$
examples.why: Using 'qubit' as a noun modifier with no preposition follows English word order. Portuguese needs 'de qubit'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The translation keeps the caveats in [33] and [62] ("não elimina esses limites", "não são 'apenas mais um' recurso de HPC"), and the core terms stay consistent: portas/circuitos quânticos, emaranhamento, superposição, SQD. A few spots still need editing. [15] turns "IBM-built Oak Ridge Summit" into "O IBM Summit, construído em Oak Ridge", which says where Summit was built but drops that IBM built it. There are also some calques: "hardware de commodities" [14], "interconexões de tempo próximo" for near-time interconnects [43], and "antecipamos um futuro próximo" [46]. In [30], "configurações" appears twice in the same sentence.

examples.source: The IBM-built Oak Ridge Summit was the first HPC resource to achieve ExaOPS
examples.translation: O IBM Summit, construído em Oak Ridge, foi o primeiro recurso de HPC a atingir ExaOPS
examples.suggested: O Summit de Oak Ridge, construído pela IBM, foi o primeiro recurso de HPC a atingir ExaOPS
examples.why: The source says IBM built Summit and that Summit is located at Oak Ridge. The translation instead says where it was built and loses the IBM attribution.

examples.source: clusters of commodity hardware
examples.translation: clusters de hardware de commodities
examples.suggested: clusters de hardware comum (de prateleira)
examples.why: This is a calque. In Portuguese, "commodities" means raw goods, not off-the-shelf hardware.

examples.source: connected via near-time interconnects
examples.translation: conectados via interconexões de tempo próximo
examples.suggested: conectados por interconexões de baixa latência (near-time)
examples.why: "Tempo próximo" is a literal rendering that a Portuguese-speaking engineer would not recognise as a term.

examples.source: we anticipate a near future where quantum processors are integrated alongside traditional HPC resources
examples.translation: antecipamos um futuro próximo em que processadores quânticos serão integrados junto com recursos tradicionais de HPC
examples.suggested: prevemos um futuro próximo em que processadores quânticos serão integrados aos recursos tradicionais de HPC
examples.why: "Antecipar" used to mean "expect" is an anglicism, and "integrados junto com" is redundant.

examples.source: listing every possible arrangement of 50 particles ... leads to configurations that grow
examples.translation: listar todas as possíveis configurações de 50 partículas ... leva a configurações que crescem
examples.suggested: listar todos os arranjos possíveis de 50 partículas ... leva a um número de configurações que cresce
examples.why: The word is repeated within one sentence, and the adjective order "possíveis configurações" reads stiffly.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the tricky last 40% (resilience levels, ZNE, PEA, PEC), and nothing would mislead a learner. A few editing slips remain. "on-premises" is calqued as "em premissas" in [14]; "premissas" means logical premises, so it should be "locais" or "on-premises". Transpiler is split between "Transpiler" ([41], [54]) and "transpilador"/"Transpilador" everywhere else. Sampler/Estimator appear in lowercase in [26] but capitalized elsewhere. "abstracted away from the user" in [42] comes out as "abstraídas para o usuário", which reads as "for the user", not "hidden from the user". There are also small calques: "menos e menos ruído" in [80] and "valor de expectativa", where "valor esperado" is the usual term.

examples.source: some of them are dedicated, on-premises systems
examples.translation: alguns deles são sistemas dedicados em premissas
examples.suggested: alguns deles são sistemas dedicados instalados localmente (on-premises)
examples.why: 'premissas' means logical premises; it is a false-friend calque of 'premises'.

examples.source: which can largely be abstracted away from the user
examples.translation: que podem em grande parte ser abstraídas para o usuário
examples.suggested: que podem, em grande parte, ficar ocultas do usuário
examples.why: 'para o usuário' flips the sense toward 'for the user'. [73] gets it right with 'abstraem ... do usuário'.

examples.source: The transpiler (which we'll discuss shortly)
examples.translation: O Transpiler (que discutiremos em breve)
examples.suggested: O transpilador (que discutiremos em breve)
examples.why: [41] and [54] keep 'Transpiler' in English, while [55]-[78] use 'transpilador', so the term is inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: Sampler and Estimator
examples.translation: o sampler e o estimator
examples.suggested: o Sampler e o Estimator
examples.why: These are product/primitive names and are capitalized everywhere else in the file ([73]-[75]).

examples.source: if there were less and less noise
examples.translation: se houvesse menos e menos ruído
examples.suggested: se houvesse cada vez menos ruído
examples.why: This is a word-for-word calque; Portuguese says 'cada vez menos'.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, including the tricky last part: the four-solutions/fifth-most-likely analysis in [105], the three error sources in [107] and the two-layers remark in [109]. None of it would mislead a learner. What a native editor would still fix is a handful of calques and inconsistencies. "virar isso ao contrário" [32], "somos mais otimistas de explorar" [11] and "plugando" [93] are calques. The parameter name is written "gamma" in [86] but "gama" in [93]/[96]. "two-local" comes out as the awkward "dois-local (de dois corpos)" [63], and the primitives appear in lowercase as "estimator ou do sampler" [89].

examples.source: We can also flip this around, and search for the minimum
examples.translation: Podemos também virar isso ao contrário e buscar o mínimo
examples.suggested: Também podemos inverter o problema e buscar o mínimo
examples.why: 'virar isso ao contrário' is a literal calque of 'flip this around'. 'inverter' is the idiomatic technical verb.

examples.source: The three use-cases we're most optimistic about exploring are:
examples.translation: Os três casos de uso sobre os quais somos mais otimistas de explorar são:
examples.suggested: Os três casos de uso que consideramos mais promissores são:
examples.why: This keeps the English syntax, and 'otimistas de explorar' is ungrammatical and stiff in Portuguese.

examples.source: We will do this by plugging in our cost function and these initial guesses into a scipy optimizer `COBYLA`.
examples.translation: Faremos isso plugando nossa função de custo e essas estimativas iniciais em um otimizador scipy `COBYLA`.
examples.suggested: Faremos isso passando nossa função de custo e essas estimativas iniciais para o otimizador `COBYLA` do scipy.
examples.why: 'plugando' is an anglicism. Also, [86] writes 'gamma' but this entry and [96] write 'gama', so the parameter name is inconsistent.

examples.source: in terms of two-local Pauli ZZ operators
examples.translation: em termos de operadores ZZ de Pauli dois-local (de dois corpos)
examples.suggested: em termos de operadores ZZ de Pauli de dois qubits (two-local)
examples.why: 'dois-local' is not Portuguese, and the gloss 'de dois corpos' is added by the translation and not in the source.

examples.source: A single primitive request of the Estimator or Sampler primitive
examples.translation: Uma única solicitação primitiva do estimator ou do sampler
examples.suggested: Uma única solicitação à primitiva Estimator ou Sampler
examples.why: Estimator and Sampler are Qiskit class names and should stay capitalized. The translation also drops the word 'primitive'.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally. Core terms are used correctly and consistently: "valores esperados de matrizes", "diagonalização quântica baseada em amostras (SQD)" and "solver quântico variacional de autovalores (VQE)", and the badge rules (at least 70% on the 20-question quiz) are preserved exactly.

The meaning holds throughout, including the teleportation and superdense-coding protocol steps, the correction table, and the takeaways on faster-than-light signalling and no-cloning. A native editor would still fix a few things. "trace out Bob's results" is rendered "rastrear" ("track"), which loses the marginalization meaning. There are two grammar slips: "Se você ver" should be "vir", and "Dado a forma" should be "Dada". "Assumption" is rendered two ways ("Suposição" in [55], "Premissa" in [115]). Smaller points: "sem explicação" gained an extra "detalhada", "not knowable" became "não seria identificável", and "um único QPU" would usually be feminine in pt.

examples.source: using `marginal_count`, you can trace out Bob's results on qubit 2.
examples.translation: usando `marginal_count`, pode rastrear os resultados de Bob no qubit 2.
examples.suggested: usando `marginal_count`, pode isolar (marginalizar) os resultados de Bob no qubit 2.
examples.why: 'Trace out' means marginalizing over the other qubits. 'Rastrear' means track or trace a path, which is the wrong sense.

examples.source: If you see `'DONE'` is displayed, you can get the result
examples.translation: Se você ver `'DONE'` exibido, pode obter o resultado
examples.suggested: Se aparecer `'DONE'`, você pode obter o resultado
examples.why: 'Se você ver' is a grammar error. The future subjunctive is 'vir'.

examples.source: Given the form:
examples.translation: Dado a forma:
examples.suggested: Dada a forma:
examples.why: The participle must agree with the feminine noun 'forma'.

examples.source: **Assumption**: Alice has two bits of information
examples.translation: **Premissa**: Alice tem dois bits de informação
examples.suggested: **Suposição**: Alice tem dois bits de informação
examples.why: Entry [55] renders the same label as 'Suposição', so the parallel protocol sections are inconsistent.

examples.source: Here we outline the procedure without explanation.
examples.translation: Aqui descrevemos o procedimento sem explicação detalhada.
examples.suggested: Aqui descrevemos o procedimento sem explicações.
examples.why: Adding 'detalhada' changes the claim slightly. The English says no explanation is given at this point.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The local/global optimizer trade-offs, the barren-plateau probability claim and the recommendations all match the English. The main problem is that "cost landscape" is rendered as "cenário da função de custo". "Paisagem" is the usual term, and in [31] the same word "cenário" also translates "scenario", so two different ideas get blurred together. There are also smaller calques: "Experimente com ..." in [35]-[37] (Portuguese "experimentar" is transitive) and "alimentar parâmetros em cálculos quânticos" in [0].

examples.source: This scenario is referred to as a barren plateau, where the cost landscape becomes progressively flatter
examples.translation: Esse cenário é chamado de platô estéril, onde o cenário da função de custo se torna progressivamente mais plano
examples.suggested: Essa situação é chamada de platô estéril, em que a paisagem da função de custo se torna progressivamente mais plana
examples.why: 'Cenário' translates both 'scenario' and 'landscape' in the same sentence. 'Paisagem (de custo)' is the conventional term for the optimization landscape.

examples.source: **Experimenting with hardware-efficient ansatz**
examples.translation: **Experimente com ansatz eficiente em hardware**
examples.suggested: **Experimente ansatz eficientes em hardware**
examples.why: Calque of 'experiment with'. In Portuguese 'experimentar' takes a direct object. The same pattern appears in [36] and [37].

examples.source: to feed parameters into quantum calculations
examples.translation: para alimentar parâmetros em cálculos quânticos
examples.suggested: para fornecer parâmetros aos cálculos quânticos
examples.why: 'Alimentar ... em' is a literal rendering of 'feed into' that a native technical writer would not use.

editor_note: The meaning holds up throughout. The forward/backward bounds, the four-hour noise-model recompute, the ~10k sampling cost and the comparison of PEC with PEC+SLC all match the English. The problems are consistency ones. "Sampling overhead" is "sobrecarga de amostragem" in [3]-[5] and then switches to "overhead de amostragem" from [100] on. "Antinoise" is "antirruído" everywhere except the [111] heading, which keeps the English "antinoise". "Primitive" is feminine "primitiva" in [27] but masculine "primitivo" in [113]/[116]. "Framework" is kept in English in [6]/[24] but becomes "estrutura" in [99]. There are also two stiff calques: "propagação reversa solta" in [12] and "mitigação de erros com consciência local" in [4].

examples.source: determine the sampling overhead
examples.translation: determinar o overhead de amostragem
examples.suggested: determinar a sobrecarga de amostragem
examples.why: Entries [3]-[5] use 'sobrecarga de amostragem'. From here on the file switches to 'overhead', so one term is rendered two ways.

examples.source: Execute the circuit of interest with antinoise
examples.translation: Executar o circuito de interesse com antinoise
examples.suggested: Executar o circuito de interesse com antirruído
examples.why: Every other entry ([7], [18], [43], [49]) uses 'antirruído'. This heading leaves the English word.

examples.source: with the `Executor` primitive
examples.translation: com o primitivo `Executor`
examples.suggested: com a primitiva `Executor`
examples.why: Entry [27] uses the feminine 'a primitiva Executor', which is the usual Qiskit pt form. The gender changes within the file.

examples.source: a loose back-propagation of the observable
examples.translation: uma propagação reversa solta do observável
examples.suggested: uma retropropagação aproximada do observável
examples.why: 'Solta' is a literal translation of 'loose' and reads oddly. 'Aproximada' carries the intended meaning of a coarse or approximate propagation.

examples.source: implementing locally aware error mitigation
examples.translation: implementar a mitigação de erros com consciência local
examples.suggested: implementar a mitigação de erros sensível à localidade
examples.why: 'Com consciência local' is a calque of 'locally aware'. A native technical writer would use 'sensível à localidade' or similar.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through and nothing would mislead a learner. The caveats (the 9^3 sampling overhead, depth "reduzida em mais da metade", optimization_level=3 as the highest preset level) are all kept. The main terminology problem is "expectation value", which is rendered throughout (entries 10, 23, 24, 32, 33) as the calque "valor de expectativa"; Portuguese quantum-computing writing normally uses "valor esperado". Two smaller wording slips: "a Primitiva Sampler" is capitalized when it shouldn't be (entry 28), and "subexperimento arbitrariamente escolhido" is stiff (entry 24).

examples.source: To simulate the expectation value of the full-sized circuit
examples.translation: Para simular o valor de expectativa do circuito em tamanho completo
examples.suggested: Para simular o valor esperado do circuito em tamanho completo
examples.why: 'Valor de expectativa' is a literal calque. The usual Portuguese term is 'valor esperado', and it should be used in every entry (10, 23, 24, 32, 33).

examples.source: with the Sampler primitive
examples.translation: com a Primitiva Sampler
examples.suggested: com a primitiva Sampler
examples.why: 'Primitiva' is a common noun and should be lowercase, as it is in entry 27 ('primitivas Qiskit').

examples.source: an example of an arbitrarily chosen subexperiment
examples.translation: um exemplo de um subexperimento arbitrariamente escolhido
examples.suggested: um exemplo de um subexperimento escolhido arbitrariamente
examples.why: This copies the English word order. In Portuguese the adverb reads more naturally after the participle.
